hook: The Nationalist leader who united China, fought Japan, then lost the mainland to Mao.

pages.x: Chiang Kai-shek was born in 1887 in Xikou, a small town in eastern China, the son of a salt merchant. He trained as a soldier in Japan, and joined the revolution that overthrew the last emperor in 1911.
In 1924 the revolutionary leader Sun Yat-sen made him head of a new military academy at Whampoa, to train officers for his Nationalist party's army.
In 1927 in Shanghai he turned on his communist allies and had thousands of them killed. It began a civil war that lasted, on and off, for 22 years.
In his Northern Expedition, from 1926 to 1928, he defeated the warlords who had carved up China, and united most of the country under a Nationalist government in Nanjing.
In December 1936 two of his own generals kidnapped him at Xi'an, and would not let him go until he agreed to stop fighting the communists and join them against Japan.
From 1937 he led China's long and bloody war against the Japanese invasion, from a wartime capital at Chongqing. In 1943 he met Roosevelt and Churchill in Cairo as one of the Allied leaders.

After Japan's defeat the civil war with Mao's communists flared again. Corruption, soaring prices and defeats cost him the country, and in 1949 he fled to Taiwan with some two million soldiers and refugees.

He ruled Taiwan under martial law until he died in 1975, still claiming to be China's rightful ruler, and thousands were jailed or executed. Its economy boomed, and after his death Taiwan became a democracy.
Chiang united China for a time and led its long war against Japan, but lost the mainland to the communists. The Republic of China he led lives on in Taiwan.
pts: Led the Nationalists and united most of China
